item.title: [jhspetersson/fselect] 0.10.5
item.description:
jhspetersson/fselect | 4483 stars| 88 forks.

| Rust | Dockerfile | Shell |

Find files with SQL-like queries

Added

  • select top N ... as a synonym for limit N

Changed

  • Matroska and WebM metadata is behind the mkv build feature, enabled by default.
  • The update-notifications build feature is no longer enabled by default.
  • Column aliases are no longer accepted after WHERE and HAVING conditions
  • Subquery columns are named after their query in output headers and error messages instead of a hash
  • DISTINCT is rejected with a hint instead of being read as a column named "distinct"
  • A doubled quote inside a quoted string ('it''s') is a literal quote
  • Missing numeric, date and boolean values are written as null in JSON output
  • Dates and times are handled by jiff instead of chrono
  • Several hash columns selected together (sha1, sha256, sha512, sha3) are computed in one read of the file
  • width, height and duration of an MP4 file come from a single parse of the file

Fixed

  • Unterminated or mismatched subquery parentheses are rejected instead of silently closed
  • Operators such as IN and BETWEEN work after a subquery in the SELECT list
  • A correlated subquery in a grouped query may only read grouping columns of the outer row
  • INTO inside a subquery is rejected with a clear message
  • EXISTS with a doubly parenthesized subquery evaluates the subquery instead of being always true
  • An invalid regular expression literal is reported once when the query is parsed instead of per file
  • A negative operand written with a space after the minus sign (size > - 1) is parsed as a number
  • An aggregate function in WHERE is rejected instead of silently matching nothing
  • GROUP BY and ORDER BY without an expression are rejected
  • A column alias may be referenced in the SELECT list before the column that declares it
  • Division by a literal zero is rejected when the query is parsed instead of per file
  • A date literal with an impossible month (2020-13-01) is rejected instead of being read as arithmetic
  • Nested aggregate functions (count(count(*))) are rejected
  • AS without an alias, or an alias inside parentheses, is rejected instead of being ignored
  • Two search roots with the same alias are rejected
  • An invalid literal unit, day count, precision or position argument of a date or string function is reported once when the query is parsed instead of per file
  • NOT without a following operator (where is_file not) is rejected instead of being ignored
  • A column name used as a function (sha1(name)) is rejected instead of being read as two columns
  • NOT IN no longer accepts a row when the list or subquery contains a NULL member and nothing matches
  • Numeric functions such as ABS, GREATEST and HEX read the byte count of fsize instead of its formatted text
  • A relative date such as 1 year ago no longer fails when it lands in January
  • A date with non-ASCII letters (2024é) is rejected instead of crashing
  • 2 days ago and similar day offsets keep the time of day across a daylight saving change
  • Comparing a boolean with a number gives the same result in either order (is_file = size and size = is_file); the boolean counts as 1 or 0
  • HAVING reads a computed right-hand operand as a number, date or boolean the same way WHERE does

item.title: [sharkdp/bat] v0.27.0
item.description:
sharkdp/bat | 61524 stars| 2316 forks.

| Rust | Shell | Batchfile | Python | Nix |

A cat(1) clone with wings.

v0.27.0

Features

  • Map .yamllint, .prettierrc and .eslintrc to YAML syntax highlighting, see #4156 (@yusufemreboyraz)
  • Map .clang-tidy to YAML syntax highlighting, see #4150 (@yusufemreboyraz)
  • Automatically build the syntax/theme cache on first run when custom themes or syntaxes are present but no cache exists yet, so newly installed dotfiles work without a manual bat cache --build. Use --no-custom-assets to opt out. Closes #4017, see #4038 (@mmustafasenoglu)
  • Add -b / --number-nonblank flag to only number non-blank lines, for cat -b compatibility. Closes #3856, see #3857 (@MeGaurav4)
  • Add a --sanitize=<auto|always|never> flag for safe display of untrusted input. It substitutes terminal-active control bytes (escape, cursor moves, charset switches, beep, etc.) and Unicode bidi / zero-width formatting characters with the Unicode replacement character (U+FFFD). Mitigates Trojan-Source-style spoofing (CVE-2021-42574). See #3729 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Map justfile, Justfile, .justfile, and *.justfile to Makefile syntax highlighting, see #3623 (@zachvalenta)
  • Map .kube/config to YAML syntax highlighting, see #3911 (@logarithmone1128)
  • Preserve --diff change markers and snip separators when --plain is set. Closes #3630, see #3643 (@mvanhorn)
  • Added support for hidden_file_extensions from .sublime-syntax files, see #3613 (@Matei02355)
  • Add word wrapping mode via --wrap=word, see #3597 (@veeceey)
  • Support configuring --terminal-width via BAT_WIDTH, see #3679 (@officialasishkumar)
  • Implement --unbuffered mode for streaming input, allowing partial lines to display immediately (e.g. tail -f | bat -u). Closes #3555, see #3583 (@mainnebula)
  • Added an initial flake.nix for a ready made development environment; see #3578 (@vorburger)
  • Add --quiet-empty (-E) flag to suppress output when input is empty. Closes #1936, see #3563 (@NORMAL-EX)
  • Improve native man pages and command help syntax highlighting by stripping overstriking, see #3517 (@akirk)
  • Add --fallback-syntax/--fallback-language to apply syntax highlighting only when auto-detection fails, see #1341 (@Xavrir)
  • Map BUILD case sensitively to Python (Starlark) for Bazel, see #3576 (@vorburger)
  • Syntax highlighting for Python files using uv as script runner in shebang #3689 (@janlarres)

Bugfixes

  • Track reverse video (SGR 7 / 27) in the ANSI style tracker so it is re-emitted like bold, dim, italic, and underline, and is no longer dropped after the first wrapped line when displaying ANSI input, see #4144 (@BlueX888)
  • Preserve buffered stdin when $LESSOPEN temporary-file mode falls back to the original input, and handle CRLF line endings on returned temp paths, see #4158 (@xgbtxy)
  • Skip cache metadata validation when --no-custom-assets is set so outdated or malformed caches do not block fallback to integrated assets, see #4157 (@xgbtxy)
  • Only show style decorations with --decorations=auto when stdout is interactive, so piped --color=always output no longer includes the header, grid, or line numbers, see #4151 (@draarivpatel-ui)
  • Break --wrap=word lines at whitespace in earlier highlighted tokens or before ANSI escape sequences instead of in the middle of a word, closes #4139, see #4140 (@mansur-akhmadi)
  • Fix bat cache --help returning exit code 1 instead of 0. Remove .arg_required_else_help(true) from the cache subcommand and show help when no arguments are provided. See #3798, #3831 and #3837 (@Amilliox)
  • Fix builtin pager (minus) not responding to search (/, ?, n, N) and navigation (PgUp, PgDown, arrows, g, G) keys. HashedEventRegister was overriding all default minus bindings instead of extending them. Add generate_default_bindings() before custom bindings. See #3831, #3798 and #3837 (@Amilliox)
  • Build the cache automatically on first run when custom themes or syntaxes are in subdirectories, see #4131 (@NotAFlightRisk)
  • Do not run filter commands from the configuration of the Git repository that contains the displayed file, see #4127 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Ignore empty --ignored-suffix values to avoid a stack overflow, see #4122 (@spicysharkco)
  • Fix --number-nonblank counting empty UTF-16 lines, see #4118 (@pcbeingused333)
  • Fix automatic cache build progress polluting stdout, see #4130 (@intertermux-code)
  • Don't emit --highlight-line escape sequences (background color or ansi theme underline) when colors are disabled with --color=never. Closes #4099, see #4100 (@DeviousCardi)
  • Fix missing colors, pager, and decorations in mintty/MSYS2 and Cygwin terminals on Windows, see #4115 (@rezamuliawijaya)
  • Make full-path --map-syntax patterns and the built-in $HOME and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME mappings work on Windows, see #4113 (@b84330808)
  • Keep configuration and BAT_OPTS active for option-like filenames after --, and report invalid configuration for help-like filenames, see #4112 (@Marve10s)
  • Keep emoji sequences together within text chunks when wrapping content, and measure their combined display width, see #4108 (@Marve10s)
  • Preserve full-path syntax mappings when removing ignored filename suffixes, see #4111 (@Marve10s)
  • Fix UTF-16 line splitting at unaligned newline bytes corrupting text and shifting line ranges, see #4110 (@Marve10s)
  • Respect NO_COLOR for the [bat error] and [bat warning] prefixes, see #4048 (@qodelicious)
  • Offer the valid --wrap value auto instead of the rejected always in the PowerShell completion, see #4070 (@ump45nose)
  • Report BAT_CONFIG_DIR in bat --diagnostic, so bug reports show a config directory that overrides $XDG_CONFIG_HOME. See #4068 (@ump45nose)
  • Ignore a UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the config file instead of treating it as part of the first argument, see #4103 (@jaeminbird)
  • Keep backslashes in the pager command on Windows, so BAT_PAGER=C:\tools\less.exe is found instead of becoming C:toolsless.exe, see #4104 (@jaeminbird)
  • Fix bat hanging forever on JavaScript (and Svelte) code where an expression is followed by a block comment, e.g. a /* x */. Closes #4080, see #4091 (@NavpreetSSidhu)
  • Fix the first line of UTF-16BE input swallowing the second line, which broke line numbers, --line-range and highlighting, see #4102 (@cindykrafft)
  • Exit quietly with status 0 instead of panicking when stdout is closed early (broken pipe) on auxiliary output paths such as --completion, --config-file, --diagnostic, --generate-config-file, --set-terminal-title and cache --build/--clear, matching the main output path since #232, closes #4034, see #4035 (@Mathjk)
  • Fix escape sequence handling in --strip-ansi and --sanitize. --sanitize no longer removes escape sequences, which could hide text, see #4024 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Report unknown languages in plain piped output, see #4001 (@ryanchou1994)
  • Track strikethrough (SGR 9 / 29) in the ANSI style tracker so it is re-emitted like bold, dim, italic, and underline, and is no longer dropped after the first highlighted token when displaying ANSI input with syntax highlighting, see #4015 (@mikehasa)
  • Allow boolean flags to be given more than once, so that a flag set in the config file can also be passed on the command line without erroring, see #3912 (@logarithmone1128)
  • Allow options that take a value (--binary, --italic-text, --nonprintable-notation, --fallback-syntax, --squeeze-limit) to be given more than once, so that a value from the config file can be overridden on the command line, see #4102 (@Huang-404-Q)
  • Use parsed CLI arguments to detect number flags, see #3908 (@cuishuang)
  • Detect binary content beyond the first line, preventing encrypted files with early line breaks from being treated as text. Closes #3554, see #3877 (@Matei02355)
  • Use the last occurrence of numbering and plain flags in combined short arguments, see #3897 (@cuishuang)
  • Avoid a spurious Cargo manifest error during installation from Git, see #3899 (@rootsec1)
  • Avoid repeated scans of long lines in Log syntax highlighting, see #3876 (@Matei02355)
  • Fix --list-languages respecting --paging=never, see #3828 (@cyphercodes)
  • Fix --sanitize passing through the bidi control characters U+200E, U+200F and U+061C, see #3862 (@lenamonj)
  • --strip-ansi: also strip 8-bit C1 introducers (U+0090, U+0098, U+009B, U+009D, U+009E, U+009F) and DCS/SOS/PM/APC sequence bodies, which previously passed through. See #3729 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Fix --ignored-suffix not falling back to first-line/shebang detection when the ignored suffix is also a registered extension (e.g. --ignored-suffix .txt on a shebang script), see #2745 and #3816 (@adnrivera)
  • Fix capacity overflow panic when printing a snip separator at --terminal-width=1 with multiple line ranges. Closes #3803, see #3804 (@leeewee)
  • Pass --no-paging to bat invocations inside the bash / zsh / fish / PowerShell shell completion scripts so that shell-level pager wiring (e.g. LESSOPEN='|-bat -f -pp %s') cannot inject ANSI escape sequences into the completion candidates. Closes #3760 (@mvanhorn)
  • Quote filenames before substituting them into $LESSOPEN / $LESSCLOSE templates, preventing shell injection when a filename contains shell metacharacters, see #3726 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Fix --list-themes unconditionally probing the terminal via OSC 10/11 even when --theme was set to an explicit value, see #3700 (regression introduced in bc42149). (@optimistiCli)
  • Fix inverted $LESSCLOSE warning so bat warns on nonzero exit, not on success. See #3654 (@cuiweixie)
  • Sanitize control characters in filenames before displaying them in the file header, error messages, and the terminal title, preventing ANSI escape injection via crafted filenames. Closes #3054, see #3691 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Report initial input read errors instead of treating them as empty input. Closes #3002, see #3706 (@lawrence3699)
  • Treat ZIP archives as binary content based on their magic header, see #3686 (@officialasishkumar)
  • Fix i686 .deb package using incorrect architecture name (i686 instead of i386), preventing installation on Debian. Closes #3611, see #3650 (@Sim-hu)
  • Fix inconsistent .deb MUSL package names (aarch64-musl used arm64 instead of musl-linux-arm64, and musleabihf target missed bat-musl prefix). Closes #3482, see #3642 (@mvanhorn)
  • Fix incorrect text width computation when using --binary=as-text with non-printable characters in caret notation, see #3640 and #3631 (@eyupcanakman)
  • Fix BAT_CONFIG_DIR pointing at system config directory causing duplicate flag errors. Closes #3589, see #3620 (@Xavrir)
  • Fix syntax highlighting for symlinked files when the symlink name has no extension but the target does. Closes #1001, see #3621 (@Xavrir)
  • Report error when pager is missing instead of silently falling back, see #3588 (@IMaloney)
  • Fix --wrap=never and -S flags being ignored when piping to pager, see #3592 (@IMaloney)
  • Fix crash with BusyBox less on Windows, see #3527 (@Anchal-T)
  • Fix bat cache --help failing with 'unexpected argument' error, see #3580 and #3560 (@NORMAL-EX)
  • --help now correctly honors --pager=builtin. See #3516 (@keith-hall)
  • --help now correctly honors custom themes. See #3524 (@keith-hall)
  • Fixed test compatibility with future Cargo build directory changes, see #3550 (@nmacl)
  • Fixed bug caused by using --plain and --terminal-width=N flags simultaneously, see #3529 (@H4k1l)
  • Fixed syntax tests path, see #3610 (@foxfromworld)
  • Fix zsh tab completion word-splitting language names containing spaces (e.g. HTML (Jinja2), Apache Conf), see #3693 (@YoshKoz)
  • Fix zsh tab completion offering invalid -l arguments (file globs, paths, hidden filenames) sourced from the second column of --list-languages. Closes #3735, see #3737 (@truffle-dev)
  • Fix usize underflow in --list-languages when --terminal-width is smaller than the longest language name, see #3812 (@greymoth-jp)
  • --sanitize=always now also sanitizes piped output. --sanitize=auto now sanitizes every file type, but only when the output is a terminal, see #4141 (@curious-rabbit)
  • Show changes in --diff mode and the change-marker column in Git repositories that use the SHA-256 object format (git init --object-format=sha256), see #4143 (@BlueX888)
  • Skip untracked files and files outside a Git repository in --diff mode instead of printing an empty frame, see #4148 (@thejesh23)
  • Recognize the end of an OSC 8 hyperlink in ANSI input, so later text is no longer wrapped in redundant hyperlink-close sequences, see #4136 (@divya0795)

Other

  • Use git version of cross. See #3533 (@OctopusET)
  • Bump MSRV to 1.88, update time crate to 0.3.47 to fix RUSTSEC-2026-0009, see #3581 (@NORMAL-EX)
  • Allow home and end keys to be used with builtin pager, see #3651 (@keith-hall)
  • Builtin syntax mapping: cleanup matcher glob parsing logic #3652 (@cyqsimon)
  • Statically link the CRT for MSVC builds via Cargo config to avoid runtime DLL dependencies. Closes #3634, see #3692 (@barry3406)
  • Replace libgit2 with a pure Rust implementation of git called gitoxide, see PR #3703 (@blinxen)
  • Document submodule initialization when rebuilding syntax and theme assets, see #3801 (@xfocus3)
  • Fix anchor case in doc/assets.md links, see #4026 (@ump45nose)
  • Pin the i686 GNU CI runner to Ubuntu 24.04 to avoid socketpair failures on Ubuntu 26.04, see #4101 (@PerchAnton)
  • Fix dead Visual C++ Redistributable link in README, see #3895 (@1t1sCooL)
  • Document StripAnsiMode and its variants in rustdoc, see #4067 (@ump45nose)

item.title: [opencontainers/runc] runc v1.6.0 -- "All's well that ends well."
item.description:
opencontainers/runc | 13589 stars| 2359 forks.

| Dockerfile | Makefile | Go | C | Shell |

CLI tool for spawning and running containers according to the OCI specification

This is the first stable release of the 1.6.z release branch of runc.
It contains a handful of fixes and a few dependency bumps, including
one fixing a medium security issue.

This release follows our release and support policy (see RELEASES.md
for more details). This means that, as of this release:

  • The runc 1.3.z (and earlier) release branches are now unsupported.
  • The runc 1.4.z release branch will now only receive high severity
    CVE fixes, and will no longer be supported in less than 6 months
    (end of April 2027).
  • The runc 1.5.z release branch will now only receive security and
    "significant" bugfixes.
  • Users are encouraged to plan migrating to runc 1.6.0 as soon as
    possible.
  • Despite this release being delayed by almost a month, users should
    still expect a runc 1.7.0 release in late April 2027.

Security

This release includes github.com/moby/sys/user v0.5.1, which fixes the
following medium-severity security issue:

  • CVE-2026-135844 allowed unbounded reads when parsing user and group
    files. In runc, a malicious image with a huge /etc/passwd could make
    runc init consume excessive memory and CPU while looking up the user's
    home directory (which is done when HOME is not set in the process
    environment). (#5631)

Added

  • THREAT_MODEL.md describes what runc does and does not consider a security
    vulnerability, to help security researchers and automated scanners. It is
    linked from SECURITY.md. (#5361, #5566)

Fixed

  • When the container does not have its own cgroup namespace, runc no longer
    mounts a new cgroup v2 filesystem instance for /sys/fs/cgroup, as doing so
    could change host cgroupfs mount options such as nsdelegate. Instead, the
    existing cgroup v2 hierarchy is bind mounted. (#5258, #5267)
  • Fixed a buffer overflow in runc init when more than 5 user namespace ID
    mappings are set using newuidmap/newgidmap (as it happens with rootless
    runc), which resulted in a failed to execv: Bad address error. Up to 340
    mappings (the kernel limit) are now supported. (#5507)
  • The bash completion is now in sync with runc commands and options, and
    a CI test ensures it stays that way. (#5299, #5568)
  • The --pidfd-socket option is now documented in runc-create(8),
    runc-exec(8) and runc-run(8) man pages. (#5568)

Changed

  • Switched to opencontainers/cgroups v0.1.2, which no longer depends on
    cilium/ebpf and, indirectly, crypto packages. The new version also fixes
    CPU quota overflow and cpu.max rounding in the systemd driver, and adds
    support for zswap unified resources. (#5612, #5623)
  • Updated dependencies: golang.org/x/sys to v0.50.0, golang.org/x/net to
    v0.63.0. (#5618, #5632)

Static Linking Notices

The runc binaries distributed with this release are statically linked with
the following GNU LGPL-2.1 licensed libraries, with runc acting
as a "work that uses the Library":

  • libseccomp

Similarly, the runc binaries distributed with this release are also
statically linked with the following MPLv2 licensed libraries,
with runc acting as a "Larger Work":

  • libpathrs

The versions of these libraries were not modified from their upstream versions,
but in order to comply with their corresponding licenses, we have attached the
complete source code for those libraries which (when combined with the attached
runc source code) may be used to exercise your rights under their respective
licenses.

However, we strongly suggest that you make use of your distribution's packages
or download them from the authoritative upstream sources, especially since
these libraries are related to the security of your containers.

item.description:
bblimke/webmock | 4047 stars| 588 forks.

| Ruby |

Library for stubbing and setting expectations on HTTP requests in Ruby.

  • Fix VCR failing to replay responses recorded with the auto_inflate feature of the http gem (#1154)

    Previously, for a real request made with HTTP.use(:auto_inflate), after_request callbacks got the inflated body together with the Content-Encoding: gzip header of the compressed one. VCR, hooked into WebMock, recorded both, and replaying the cassette raised Zlib::DataError: incorrect header check, because the feature tried to inflate the body again. With VCR's decode_compressed_response option, recording raised Zlib::GzipFile::Error instead.

    Callbacks now get the inflated body without the Content-Encoding header, as they do for a body that Net::HTTP inflates. A Content-Length header, when the response has one, gives the size of the inflated body. The response the client returns is unchanged, and so are the headers of a response with an empty body, such as one to a HEAD request.

    A cassette recorded this way replays the response with those headers, while the real response keeps the headers of the compressed body.

    This doesn't cover a client that inflates with a subclass of the feature, or responses returned by the caching feature of http 6. Callbacks get those as before.

    Cassettes recorded with older versions that have the Content-Encoding header on an inflated body still fail. Record them again, or remove that header from their responses. Their Content-Length is still that of the compressed body.

item.title: [pimalaya/himalaya] v3.0.0
item.description:
pimalaya/himalaya | 7736 stars| 274 forks.

| Rust | Shell | Nix |

CLI to manage emails

Himalaya 3 is a low-level CLI over a unified mail API: the same commands on every backend, the protocol-specific ones beside them, plain text for a glance and --json for scripts, frontends and AI agents. Daily-mail comfort (tables, colours, relative dates, rich composition) moves to frontends such as himalaya-tui and to mml, and the offline side to the pimdir store Neverest syncs, which Himalaya reads and queues its writes into.

The wizard, the m2dir backend and the display options are gone, an unknown configuration key fails the load, and every failure carries a stable code. MIGRATION.md lists what to act on when upgrading from 2.x.

Added

  • Added the account-level tls table (tls.provider, tls.rustls.crypto, tls.cert, tls.client.cert, tls.client.key), inherited field by field by every network backend.

    A backend's own tls wins, so one trusted certificate reaches IMAP, SMTP, ManageSieve, JMAP, Gmail and Microsoft Graph alike.

  • Added tls.client.cert and tls.client.key to every network backend, a client certificate presented for mutual TLS.

    native-tls reads a PKCS#8 key only.

  • Added maildir.layout, fs by default or maildir++ for a Dovecot or Courier store.

    The root is the inbox, .a.b lists as a/b, and a level holding a dot is refused.

  • Added message.reply.posting-style and message.forward.posting-style, global or per account, the style used without --posting-style ([#772]).

  • Added the first-run welcome: at a terminal without a configuration, a command prints the missing path and the commands copying config.sample.toml in place, then exits 1.

    Under --json or with stderr piped, the error names the path and the sample instead.

  • Added config.sample.toml to the Nix package and the release archives as share/doc/himalaya/config.sample.toml, which install.sh installs under its prefix.

  • Added a stable code to the JSON failure object for the failures a caller is expected to act on, null otherwise.

    json-schema himalaya-error describes the object and lists every code.

  • Added the item and mailbox codes message-not-found, mailbox-not-found, message-unreadable, mailbox-unreadable, mailbox-duplicate, message-too-complex, thread-not-found, identity-not-found and submission-not-found.

  • Added the server refusal codes permission-denied, quota-exceeded, rate-limited (a Google daily quota included) and recipient-refused.

  • Added the usage codes usage-invalid, capability-missing, search-invalid, search-unsupported, page-token-invalid, stdin-taken, attachment-too-large, attachment-invalid and request-origin.

  • Added the account codes account-missing, account-default-missing, account-default-several and backend-not-built, the last naming the cargo feature to rebuild with.

  • Added the pimdir codes io-pimdir gives a store, its queue and its search index.

    Store: store-version, store-uncreated, store-foreign, store-corrupt, store-not-current, store-hash-algo, store-busy, store-owned, store-staging, store-in-flight, store-exposed, store-reset, source-empty, store-account-ambiguous, store-account-unknown, sync-version, lock-replaced.

    Queue and index: body-pending, item-duplicate, flag-invalid, action-malformed, conflict-unread, unsupported, no-performer, ambiguous-performer, row-not-found, confirmation-required, index-missing, index-outdated, index-version, index-zone-unknown, index-fts5-missing, query-refused, query-unanswerable, tag-refused.

  • Added errors to envelope list|search, mailbox list, flag add|set|remove and message copy|move|delete, one item error {id, code, error, sources} per item the command could not list or act on.

    A non-empty errors exits 3. In text each entry prints as an Error: line after the items.

  • Added a JSON Schema for every command, himalaya-error for the failure object, and .events schemas for what imap raw and sieve raw print before their result.

  • Added total to envelope list --json, how many messages the mailbox holds, null on Gmail and Microsoft Graph and for envelope search.

  • Added --page-token to envelope list|search and jmap email|mailbox|submission query, taking back the nextPage a page printed, null on the last page.

    It is refused beside --page, and a token no listing printed fails page-token-invalid.

  • Added --page-token to msgraph messages list, mail-folders list and mail-folders child-folders, following as is the Graph next link they print as nextPage.

    A query option beside it is refused (exit 2), the link carrying the query.

  • Added a library target, which himalaya-tui pins by git revision to run Himalaya's commands in-process, with no semver promise beyond the CLI grammar and --json.

  • Added himalaya repl, a session running one command per line over clients connected once for the session.

    Piped, every line gets exactly one answer; a line setting -a, -c, --log-level or -b, or reading stdin (stdin-taken), is refused.

  • Added himalaya mcp, a Model Context Protocol server over stdio exposing the account's unified API as tools named after their command.

    Only the reading tools are listed by default: --allow-write adds the writes and --allow-send the sends, which keep no copy without --allow-write.

  • Added the MCP tool attachment_download and the attach-data argument of message_compose, message_reply and message_forward ([#805], [#806]).

    Both refuse a part over himalaya mcp --max-attachment-size, 10 MiB by default, coded attachment-too-large.

  • Added account capability, listing what the account serves of the unified API: per capability its backend, its level (full, partial, server, none) and the detail.

  • Added a capability table per backend: a unified command reaching a capability its backend declares none is refused before connecting, coded capability-missing.

    The --help of every unified command ends with a generated Backends: footer listing those levels.

  • Added mailbox create, mailbox rename and mailbox delete to the unified API, on every backend.

    A delete takes the messages the mailbox holds; on pimdir each is queued for the sync engine.

  • Added the important and junk flags (RFC 8457 $Important, $Junk) to flag add|set|remove.

    Graph refuses junk, Gmail's junk is the SPAM label, and Maildir needs maildir.keywords.dovecot.

  • Added vacation get and vacation set, reading and changing the auto-reply on JMAP and Gmail, whatever configured backend holds the mail.

    IMAP refuses it, naming himalaya sieve.

  • Added message parse [EML], printing the message read view of a raw message from a file or stdin with no account, --part and --section writing one part.

  • Added --stdout to attachment download, writing one part's decoded bytes to stdout, or {id, mime, filename, size, data} with data in base64 under --json.

  • Fixed a header field whose name holds a blank being read as the field it spells, and a body line being read as From: after an unusual Date zone.

  • Fixed flag add|set|remove with answered or draft on Gmail and Microsoft Graph, and message add -f answered|draft on Gmail, reporting success while changing nothing: they fail with capability-missing.

  • Fixed flag set on Gmail failing whole by naming the DRAFT label.

  • Fixed Gmail date clauses being off by a day: each bound is sent as the Unix seconds of the UTC day.

  • Fixed a JMAP date clause under not or or being checked as if it stood alone: it reads the server's received date.

  • Fixed hasAttachment reading differently per backend: IMAP, Maildir, mbox and pimdir follow one rule ([#802]).

    Any disposition but inline counts; with none, a part counts unless text, multipart or named by a Content-ID; a signature or an encrypted part never does.

  • Fixed account list never naming pimdir among an account's backends.

  • Fixed account check refusing an account declaring only a pimdir block: the store is opened, its mailboxes listed and a producer probed.

  • Fixed a pimdir add or send writing its body before the store accepted the write, so a collector could delete it or a refused write leave it behind.

  • Fixed body search clauses never matching on a pimdir account.

  • Fixed a pimdir flag change queueing a row for a message that already shows the result.

  • Fixed flag add and flag remove on a pimdir account replacing every flag of a message whose flags the sync engine never read: they fail saying so.

  • Fixed flag remove on a pimdir account missing a flag the store holds in another spelling (\seen, Thunderbird's Junk).

  • Fixed a pimdir write on several messages staging the first ones before failing on a later one: the rows are one batch, all staged or none.

  • Fixed Maildir mailboxes being named by their last path segment: they are named by their path relative to maildir.root (himalaya-tui#22).

  • Fixed control and bidi characters from messages and servers reaching the terminal through the plain output.

  • Fixed pimdir queue details in the unified outputs: envelope list reports no queued count and a send prints no queueId, pimdir queue list showing what is queued.

  • Fixed message compose, reply and forward writing a Message-ID on the machine's hostname: it sits on the domain of the From address.

  • Fixed message copy|move on IMAP without MOVE reporting a copied message as not found when the COPYUID cannot be read, such as Mailo's UIDVALIDITY 0 ([#781]).

  • Fixed a raw message piped on stdin being cut at its first line that is not valid UTF-8 and still reported as sent or saved: stdin and message files are read whole as bytes ([#786]).

  • Fixed the plain output of the writes, sieve get|list|capability and jmap query not ending with a newline, and jmap email parse running its bodies together ([#777]).

  • Fixed the envelope search query errors carrying ANSI colour escapes, even inside the --json error string.

  • Fixed message delete in a JMAP trash destroying an email other mailboxes held too.

  • Fixed the writes on JMAP, Gmail and Microsoft Graph acting on an id of another mailbox: an id counts only when its message is in the mailbox given.

    On Graph, message delete -m trash given the id of a message in another folder deleted it for good.

  • Fixed message delete in the trash reporting every id given as deleted: it counts the ids the trash held.

  • Fixed flag add|set|remove and message copy|move|delete running on no id, and acting twice on a repeated one.

  • Fixed Maildir and mbox writes given an unknown id among known ones failing part-way: every id is looked up before the first write.

  • Fixed a Maildir store listing failing on a plain file beside its folders (dovecot-uidlist), and listing phantom mailboxes through a symlink back to a folder.

  • Fixed the Maildir info flags being written out of ASCII order (:2,SF for :2,FS), and an experimental :1, info section being read as flags.

  • Fixed a missing maildir.root or mbox.root listing as an empty store: it fails naming the root.

  • Fixed the Maildir and mbox mailbox writes taking a blank name or one holding a control character, and creating over or renaming onto an existing Maildir.

  • Fixed maildir delete and a Thunderbird-layout mbox delete removing the mailboxes held under the one deleted, and the Maildir root being deletable: both are refused.

  • Fixed a Thunderbird-layout mbox rename orphaning the .sbd directory of its children: it moves with the mbox.

  • Fixed an mbox flag write leaving Thunderbird's X-Mozilla-Status and X-Mozilla-Keys out of step.

  • Fixed mbox reads carrying the Status, X-Status, X-Keywords, X-Mozilla-* and Content-Length fields the store writes, so message read --raw gives back the message added.

  • Fixed the mbox commands deleting or renaming the spool the mail system delivers to: it is refused, as IMAP refuses it for INBOX.

  • Fixed INBOX on mbox without mbox.inbox addressing a missing file of that name below the root: it fails naming mbox.inbox.

  • Fixed mbox listing and appending to files that are no mbox: a non-empty file not opening on a From_ line is left out and refused.

  • Fixed an mboxcl or mboxcl2 Content-Length running past a message boundary merging the messages after it under one id.

  • Fixed a busy mbox lock failing uncoded: a lock held past mbox.lock.timeout fails store-busy, and a denied dotlock names mbox.lock.dotlock = false.

  • Fixed message delete on Maildir moving the trash's messages to the trash again when the trash was named by path or alias.

  • Fixed a copy or move between Maildirs carrying dovecot keyword letters verbatim: with maildir.keywords.dovecot they are renamed through the target's file.

  • Fixed a Maildir that cannot be searched reading as missing cur/ subdirectory: the permission error names the path.

  • Fixed the local body search clause matching case-insensitively in ASCII only.

  • Fixed the client-side sort of Maildir, mbox, pimdir, Gmail, Microsoft Graph and IMAP's fallback to follow RFC 5256: base subject, first address's mailbox, case ignored.

  • Fixed an IMAP keyword search naming a registered keyword in another case being sent as typed: junk sends KEYWORD $Junk.

  • Fixed IMAP searches negating a group or an address clause, which iCloud answered wrongly: negations are pushed onto single keys.

  • Fixed a UID Fastmail's SORT lists twice being listed twice.

  • Fixed imap list sending a non-ASCII pattern unencoded and an LSUB pattern unquoted, which iCloud refuses.

  • Fixed imap fetch --structure printing the server's uppercase MIME types.

  • Fixed imap copy and imap move saying the messages were copied or moved when no COPYUID said so.

  • Fixed imap thread on a server without the algorithm's THREAD= capability failing with a parse error: it is refused with capability-missing.

  • Fixed a JMAP write failing whole on one refused id: each is an errors entry coded by its SetError type, the others written.

  • Fixed message add, a save and a send on a JMAP server forbidding duplicates (Fastmail) failing on bytes the account holds: the existing email is filed or submitted.

  • Fixed the JMAP set and method errors dropping the type, description and arguments the server sent.

  • Fixed setting the JMAP vacation response on Fastmail failing after the update was applied.

  • Fixed a JMAP mailbox name matching none being sent to the server, and one two mailboxes carry resolving to the first: both are refused.

  • Fixed jmap email read printing server values unsanitized and running two emails together.

  • Fixed the JMAP query commands returning the objects in the server's order rather than the query's.

  • Fixed jmap email update dropping the patches a replacement overrode and accepting no change: both are refused.

  • Fixed a Gmail search pattern widening the search with the operators it held: each pattern is a literal.

  • Fixed a Gmail reply or forward added or sent outside its thread: it carries the parent's threadId.

  • Fixed a Gmail mailbox naming no label failing with Gmail's error: it is refused naming the value.

  • Fixed the Gmail snippets printing their <b> marks and HTML entities.

  • Fixed Gmail ids, label ids and addresses reaching the request paths unencoded.

  • Fixed the Microsoft Graph roles dropping at random, -m sent then reaching Graph as a folder id.

  • Fixed mailbox list on Microsoft Graph leaving out the nested folders and every folder past the first page: a nested one is named by its path (Projets/Alpha).

  • Fixed a Microsoft Graph mailbox naming no folder being sent into the request path: it is refused, and every id is percent-encoded.

  • Fixed the Microsoft Graph envelopes being dated by arrival: the date is the Date: header, else the arrival.

  • Fixed a Microsoft Graph search pattern holding KQL syntax widening the search: each word is a quoted KQL phrase, a phrase one quoted string.

  • Fixed flag set on Microsoft Graph leaving the categories it did not name.

  • Fixed msgraph messages list --search failing on a value holding : or -.

  • Fixed msgraph attachments list listing the first page alone: it follows every next link.

  • Fixed an attached message/rfc822 being written base64, which RFC 2046 forbids, and a forward dropping the Content-Type parameters of the source's attachments.

  • Fixed a composed single-part message not ending with a line break, a quoted empty line carrying a trailing blank, and the reply or forward JSON template carrying CRLF line breaks.

Security

  • Bumped rustls to 0.23.46, fixing RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to RUSTSEC-2026-0349: TLS secrets exposed by Debug, a downgrade to classical key exchange, and an unbounded certificate decompression.
  • Bumped ctutils to 0.4.6, rustls-webpki to 0.103.16 and webpki-root-certs to 1.0.11, fixing RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383 and RUSTSEC-2026-0385.
  • Fixed IMAP LOGIN and AUTHENTICATE logging credentials at trace level.
  • Fixed a server making Himalaya buffer without end: an HTTP response head is capped at 64 KiB, a body at 256 MiB, and a STARTTLS response line is capped too.
  • Fixed a SCRAM server announcing fewer than 4096 or more than five million iterations being accepted.

item.title: [meta/flow] v0.343.0
item.description:
meta/flow | 22323 stars| 1894 forks.

| Shell | JavaScript | Makefile | Ruby | CSS | Vim Snippet | TypeScript | Rust | RenderScript | MDX |

Adds static typing to JavaScript to improve developer productivity and code quality.

Likely to cause new Flow errors:

  • void follows TypeScript semantics by default and is distinct from undefined. experimental.ts_void only accepts true. Run flow codemod migrate-to-ts-void to help migrate existing code.
  • Two instantiations of an object type with an index signature are now compared by their index signatures, which can surface errors that were missed.
  • Refinements of component and hook props, and other read-only unions, now look into type alias and Values members; this can surface errors that were missed.
  • Exponential-spread errors no longer name the same union operand twice. An error for a spread with a maybe-typed operand can be reported at another operand, as it is for the explicit union.
  • Spreads, Readonly, Partial, React configs and object rest no longer drop the members of a union or intersection that contains another one, which can surface missed errors.
  • A generic or opaque value passed for a T | null | void parameter is narrowed as for ?T: T no longer takes in the null and void of its bound or supertype.
  • Spread arguments of calls are now contextually typed by the params they fill, like plain arguments, so array literals and callbacks in spread position keep their precision and no longer need annotations. A spread argument can now report the errors the same expression gets as a plain argument.
  • new of a class whose TypeScript declaration declares a constructor now gives the instance instead of any
  • A type import("m").X read from another file is no longer any when X is a type or has type arguments, and is the instance type when X is a class, also a class merged with a namespace.
  • A class extending an intersection, such as tsc's mixin output, now inherits from what its construct signatures return, with the whole intersection as its statics.
  • A call can leave out the argument for a trailing element of a fixed-length tuple rest param that accepts undefined, like g() for g(...args: [x: void]). Too few or too many arguments for such a rest param are reported as for params (requires another argument, extra-arg) instead of invalid-tuple-arity.

New Features:

  • Library declare-module blocks will now go through declaration merging.

Notable bug fixes:

  • Props can narrow the event of a React event handler they inherit, as in TypeScript.
  • Recursive type aliases whose type arguments grow as object, intersection or template literal types no longer hit the recursion limit or overflow the stack.
  • Fixed stale errors and a crash after rechecks where a change reaches checked files through node_modules, or a file's imports stop resolving
  • Fixed stale duplicate module provider errors after a new provider takes over a Haste module
  • Fixed missing and stale package.json parse errors after rechecks
  • Values of an opaque type's lower bound now flow into the opaque type after an operation narrows it, when they fit the narrowed type.
  • Under experimental.ts_void, a function that returns no value in one branch of a conditional no longer drops the annotation hint of the other branch.
  • Refinements, such as sentinel property checks, in and typeof, now narrow an opaque type's upper bound and keep the opaque type, as they do for a type parameter.
  • A type parameter that a call gives no evidence for no longer mentions the other type parameters of the signature in its inferred type.
  • When library files declare overloads of the same interface method, the overloads of the one merged later, such as a [libs] file over a builtin, are tried first.
  • A library in [libs] can override a declaration of a bundled .d.ts builtin, as it can for the other builtins.
  • Builtin overloads are tried in TypeScript's order, and Flow's fallback overloads, such as toSpliced<S>, after TypeScript's.
  • Changing a file in an import cycle of two files rechecks the files that depend on the cycle
  • A null or undefined argument for a T | null | void parameter gives T an empty bound, as for ?T.
  • Implicit instantiation no longer infers null | void from a T | null | void value whose T is not inferred yet.
  • An element passed to a prop of type (renders T) | null infers its type arguments from T, as for ?renders T or an optional prop.
  • With experimental.normalize_intersections, an intersection of unions with null and void members is normalized as one of maybe types is.
  • An interface in a declare namespace can extend another member through the namespace's name without the namespace becoming any
  • Rechecks no longer miss errors in the dependents of a file whose require switches between modules that a library declares.
  • Overloaded generic methods declared in TypeScript are compared with their type parameters erased, as in TypeScript.
  • Omit and other object type utilities no longer give an interface's index signature value to props declared elsewhere on its extends chain, e.g. an inherited onFocus when the interface has a [key: `data-${string}`] signature.
  • Error messages no longer print ? for a type with many overloads of a method.
  • Fixed a crash on a mapped type whose keys refer to the mapped type
  • Implicit instantiation infers type arguments through a conditional type whose check type indexes a type parameter, e.g. Lexical's Klass<T>
  • A type parameter of a TypeScript-declared generic that no part of a call reaches takes its default or bound, as in TypeScript, instead of being reported as underconstrained.
  • Exported mapped types and keyof over intersection keys such as string & {} no longer fail signature verification
  • A conditional type kept abstract over a type parameter now sees the type parameter narrowed by the extends type in its true branch
  • keyof and mapped types over a class declared in a .d.ts file now include its methods and inherited members.
  • typeof M.X and typeof import("m").X read a value that M exports with export type, as in TypeScript.
  • new on a Class of Readonly<I>, Partial<I> or another sliced interface with a constructor method no longer reports that constructor is missing.
  • this in the type parameter bound of a declare class method no longer errors with illegal-this.
  • A tuple type can end with a spread of a type parameter bounded by a union or intersection of arrays, or of an undecided conditional type whose branches are arrays
  • In a tuple type written in TypeScript, spreads of arrays followed by other spreads of arrays or optional elements become one rest element, as in TypeScript
  • Read-write elements of TypeScript tuples, including tuple types with spreads, are now compared covariantly, as in TypeScript.
  • Class and interface declarations accept getters and setters with computed keys, such as get [Symbol.toStringTag]()
  • Fixed a stack overflow on recursive conditional types that stay undecided over a type parameter, like the path types of react-hook-form
  • A computed key in a type can name a value imported with import type, as in TypeScript
  • Recursive type aliases whose type arguments grow as spread tuple types no longer overflow the stack
  • export default <name> inside a library declare module, as written in TypeScript .d.ts files, now declares the module's default export.
  • A type parameter bounded by keyof T can index an object keyed by keyof T, such as Record<keyof T, V>, when T has no object bound
  • An error about an argument from a spread whose type is written in another file is reported at the call instead of in that file.
  • Fixed stack overflows and recursion limit errors on property lookups through classes whose base reaches the class itself.
  • typeof and keys in types read the value of an export that is both a type and a value through import type, as in TypeScript
  • A homomorphic mapped type over an intersection with an array or tuple member, such as a type parameter bounded by Iterable<unknown> & ReadonlyArray<unknown>, no longer errors
  • A call of a TypeScript generic under the hint of an enclosing generic call, such as useState(() => f()), gives a type parameter that nothing reaches its default or bound, as in TypeScript.
  • Fixed the constructor and member precedence of a class extending a mixin applied to a class, and restored the error codes for classes extending other intersections.

Misc:

  • Errors about the keys of an intersection name the union of its keys.

IDE:

  • Hover on a type alias looks through aliases of other aliases, and Go to Definition on a qualified type, like M.X with import * as M or React.Node, goes to the member's declaration instead of staying on the reference or going to a global with the same name
  • Hover and error messages print a type declared in a library declare namespace under its qualified name, like React.MixedElement or Intl.NumberFormatOptions
  • Fixed autocomplete, go-to-definition and hover for members of a class extending an intersection or another value with construct signatures.

Library Definitions:

  • Iterator, Iterable and IterableIterator now default TReturn and TNext to any, as in TypeScript.
  • IteratorObject now defaults TReturn and TNext to unknown, as in TypeScript.
  • Built-in iterators (arrays, maps, sets, strings, enum members()) return undefined when done, as in TypeScript with strict.
  • Add the react/jsx-runtime and react/jsx-dev-runtime modules and React's FunctionComponentElement and DetailedReactHTMLElement types from @types/react

item.title: [doitsujin/dxvk] Version 3.2
item.description:
doitsujin/dxvk | 18605 stars| 1368 forks.

| C | C++ | Meson | GLSL | Shell |

Vulkan-based implementation of D3D8, 9, 10 and 11 for Linux / Wine

Present timing

If sufficiently supported by the compositor and graphics driver, VK_EXT_present_timing can now be used to achieve more consistent frame pacing in the following scenarios:

  • Running a game in full-screen mode with a non-native refresh rate. Since we cannot perform mode switches on Wayland, we have to emulate the lower refresh rate.
  • Using the built-in frame rate limiter via the dxvk.maxFrameRate config option.

Vertical synchronization must be enabled for this to work in all cases. If available, timing feedback from the present timing extension will also be used to implement DXGI frame statistics.

This feature requires using either a recent Gamescope build with ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI=1, or a Wayland-enabled Proton build (e.g. Proton-GE) on top of a Wayland compositor with support for the commit-timing-v1 protocol. Upstream winewayland currently does not work properly on all setups, and XWayland as well as Windows do not sufficiently support timing.

Note: For games that come with their own built-in frame rate limiter to e.g. 60 FPS, it may be useful to manually set e.g. DXVK_CONFIG="dxvk.maxFrameRate=60" for consistent pacing on higher-refresh displays.

Bug fixes and Improvements

  • Rewrote and simplified the Reflex implementation. This fixes issues with some games being locked to 10 FPS with Reflex enabled.
    Note: Using at least driver version 620.70.06 is recommended to avoid frame pacing issues in some games.
  • Improved VRAM eviction logic. This should help performance in various games on VRAM-constained setups. (PR #6006)
  • Updated libdisplay-info in order to fix HDR detection on some devices, such as the ROG Ally.
  • Fixed various long-standing VR issues that could occationally lead to stale images being presented.
  • Disabled VK_EXT_descriptor_heap on AMD's Windows driver due to reported issues. (#5837)
    Note: This will considerably regress CPU-bound performance on RDNA3/4 GPUs. Users can manually re-enable the feature via dxvk.conf for games where it works.
  • Improved behaviour D3D11 resource uploads in order to reduce stuttering in some cases.
  • Implemented support for D3D11 target-independent rasterization with single-sampled render targets on drivers that support VK_NV_framebuffer_mixed_samples.
    Note: The corresponding AMD extension also works, but is less accurate.
  • Improved shader code generation in various cases.
  • Fixed an issue where render target clears involving shared images were not performed correctly.
  • Fixed an issue where DXGI back buffers would contain stale data when using incremental presentation. (#5919)
    This potentially affects desktop applications using DirectComposition.
  • 7 Days to Die: Fixed intermittent stuttering on weaker GPUs.
  • Aniimo: Fixed shader compiler crash when loading into the game.
  • Deadlock: Worked around a GPU hang on Nvidia when using certain hero abilities.
  • Fallout New Vegas: Changed GPU override so that not all GPUs are reported as a Radeon 6700 XT.
  • Quantum Break: Fixed regression that would cause visual artifacts with specific render resolutions.
  • Ridiculous Space Battles: Fixed point size calculation for particles.
  • Sid Meier's Pirates!: Fixed broken color space conversion with some D3D9 video formats. (#6007)
  • Supreme Commander: Forged Alliance: Added D3D9 Multihead support for multi-monitor setups. (PR #6024)

Dear ImGui: Bloat-free Graphical User interface for C++ with minimal dependencies

Dear ImGui v1.93.1 🔧

✋ Reading the changelog is a good way to keep up to date with whaat Dear ImGui has to offer, and will give you ideas of some features that you've been ignoring until now!

As well as various paid/corporate licenses to imgui_test_engine supporting the project.

Changes in v1.93.1 (since v1.93.0)

This is a general maintenance release.

🆘 v1.93.0 has a much reworked ImDrawList system.
🆘 v1.92.8 has a signature change for the trailing optional parameters of ImDrawList::AddRect(), AddPolyline(), PathStroke(). C++ users should be notified at compile-time, but languages without type-checking may only be notified at runtime. Read v1.92.8 if using non a C++ language. Consider enabling IMGUI_DISABLE_OBSOLETE_FUNCTIONS from time to time to get rid of obsolete calls.

Breaking Changes

Autumn cleanup of stuff marked obsolete more than two years ago:

  • Commented out legacy names/functions which were obsoleted in 1.90.7 (May 2024);
    • ImGuiMod_Shortcut --> ImGuiMod_Ctrl (since 1.90.7 it maps to Cmd on macOS)
  • Commented out legacy names/functions which were obsoleted in 1.90.9 (July 2024);
    • ImGuiCol_TabActive --> ImGuiCol_TabSelected
    • ImGuiCol_TabUnfocused --> ImGuiCol_TabDimmed
    • ImGuiCol_TabUnfocusedActive --> ImGuiCol_TabDimmedSelected
  • Commented out legacy names/functions which were obsoleted in 1.91.0 (July 2024);
    • ImGuiSelectableFlags_DontClosePopups --> ImGuiSelectableFlags_NoAutoClosePopups
    • PushButtonRepeat(bool repeat) --> PushItemFlag(ImGuiItemFlags_ButtonRepeat, repeat)
    • PopButtonRepeat() --> PopItemFlag()
    • PushTabStop(bool tab_stop) --> PushItemFlag(ImGuiItemFlags_NoTabStop, !tab_stop);
    • PopTabStop() --> PopItemFlag()
  • Commented out legacy names/functions which were obsoleted in 1.91.1 (Sept 2024);
    • io.GetClipboardTextFn --> platform_io.Platform_GetClipboardTextFn
    • io.SetClipboardTextFn --> platform_io.Platform_SetClipboardTextFn
    • io.ClipboardUserData --> platform_io.Platform_ClipboardUserData
  • Please also try to get rid of calls to GetContentRegionMax(), GetWindowContentRegionMin() and GetWindowContentRegionMax() will may be removed soon-ish: you should not ever need those functions. See #7838.

Other Changes

Style:

  • StyleColorsDark(): tweaked WindowBg, PopupBg, ChildBg to be darker than in 1.93.0.
  • Added style.SymbolArrowSizeFactor, style.SymbolArrowThicknessFactor to tweak the shape and look of arrows. Made default arrow stroked. (#5233, #2431, #2235, #6730, #8243)( Legacy arrow: size: (0.60f,0.70f), thickness: 0.0f, New arrow: size: (0.72f,0.40f), thickness: 0.30f)

Windows:

  • Using SetNextWindowPos() with a pivot while a window is hidden and measuring size will still apply temporary position until size is figured out. (#9568)

TreeNode:

  • TreeNodeGetOpen(): added flags parameter to allow passing ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_DefaultOpen or ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Leaf. (#9569, #9592, #3823, #9251) [@adalisk-emikhaylov, @Yaki-Blake]
  • CollapsingHeader(): avoid extending frame boundaries by WindowPadding.x*0.5f on each side: it is inconsistent and tends to exhibits issues in various setups (that extension has been here since 1.42). (#9181, #6170)
  • Fixed combining ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Framed and ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_SpanLabelWidth.

Popups:

  • Modals: fixed an assert displaying a modal in an environment where io.DisplayFramebufferScale is not an integer (regression in 1.93.0). (#9598)

Tables:

  • Added "Reset->Reset Sizes" context-menu option. (#9523, #9605)
  • Fixed various border overshooting issues, some mostly visible with transparent borders and under specific conditions: (#4678)
    • On non-scrolling tables, inner horizontal borders slightly overlapped outer vertical ones with certain settings.
    • On non-scrolling tables, clamping lower border coordinates to stay within visible range (no visible change, but it makes ImDrawCmd AABB more sensible).
    • Fixed vertical inner borders slightly overlapping bottom outer border.
  • Fixed various issues using ImGuiTableFlags_NoHostExtendX/_NoHostExtendY:
    • Fixed selectable highlight straying off the X2/Y2 clipping limit.
    • Fixed parent window work rectangle affecting the Y2 clipping limit.
    • Fixed the Y2 clipping limit overlapping bottom outer border.
  • Fixed layout of items submitted while in horizontal layout mode (e.g. a menu bar). BeginTable() resets layout mode to vertical. (#9589) [@themd]

Multi-Select:

  • Fixed ImGuiSelectionBasicStorage::GetNextSelectedItem() reading one past the end of storage when trailing items are unselected (#9604) [@MilosLord]

Drags:

  • Fixed handling of ImGuiSliderFlags_WrapAround: value could temporarily escape the range when dragging fast. (#9612, #9611, #7749) [@swayie, @ocornut]

Checkbox:

  • Indeterminate/mixed value inner rectangle never has rounding, to reduce confusion with a radio button. (#5518, #5677, #6865, #2644)

ColorEdit:

  • ColorButton, ColorEdit, ColorPicker: fixed an issue rendering colors when inside a BeginDisabled(false) block, caused by the alpha cancelling-out code in 1.93.0. (#9511, #9613, #9614) [@tksuoran]

Fonts:

  • Detect if the parameters leading AddFontDefault() to implicitly select either AddFontDefaultBitmap() or AddFontDefaultVector() have changed between init time and first frame. (#9591)

Misc:

  • Added IsItemDisabled() convenience helper. (#9127, #9636, #4675) (same as GetItemFlags() & ImGuiItemFlags_Disabled).
  • ImVec2: added a check for cases where a custom IM_VEC2_CLASS_EXTRA macro adds an extra operator= to ImVec2. This isn't supported but should not be needed as you should have a constructor to convert from your type to ImVec2.
  • Updated stb_textedit 1.14->1.15.
    • InputText: Up/PageUp on the first line now moves the cursor to the beginning of the line, including when extending a selection. [@blackedout01]
  • Updated stb_truetype 1.26->1.27.
    • Fonts: fixed incorrect glyph mapping with certain character maps, loading fonts with only a Microsoft Symbol character map, and rendering scaled composite glyphs.
    • Fixed an out-of-bounds read with single-point off-curve contours.
  • Updated stb_rect_pack 1.01->1.02.
